additional_requirements: manic_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type is characterized by a combination of mood episodes (manic and often major depressive) and psychotic symptoms such as delusions or hallucinations, with psychotic features present for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms. Over the long term, mood and psychotic symptoms tend to be intertwined, with periods of relative stability punctuated by relapses that impair social and occupational functioning. It is distinguished from bipolar disorder with psychotic features by the persistence of psychosis outside of mood episodes, and from schizophrenia by the sustained presence of mood episodes meeting full criteria. Course is typically chronic, with variable insight, and exacerbations are often associated with psychosocial stressors, sleep disruption, and changes in role functioning or support systems.

patient.stressor: About two and a half years ago, Granville was promoted to lead a high‑stakes, organization‑wide IT migration that coincided with his push to study for PMP and CISSP exams, coaching youth teams, and maintaining a demanding outdoor and church schedule. Initially he thrived on the pressure and long hours, but as project deadlines slipped and a critical security incident drew scrutiny from senior leadership, his sleep and work–life boundaries deteriorated and his behavior became increasingly erratic at the office and in community roles. Over the following months, his once‑meticulous planning gave way to disorganized initiatives, conflicts with colleagues, and missed family commitments, culminating in HR and his supervisor expressing concern about his judgment and reliability after several alarming episodes during late‑night work sessions. His wife, worried by his drastic change and the impact on his job and community standing, arranged an urgent psychiatric evaluation after he arrived home from work insisting that he was uniquely chosen to protect the organization’s network from a vaguely defined, ever‑present cyber threat despite mounting evidence that his decisions were putting systems and relationships at risk.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I’ve been tapped for something huge at work and in town, like I’m the only one who really understands what’s going on and everyone else just needs to catch up to me.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Even when my boss and HR sat me down and showed me emails and logs proving no one was spying on me, I still knew in my gut that certain people in senior leadership had been planting bugs in our systems and in my office to monitor me specifically because they’re threatened by what I know about the network vulnerabilities.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: Pretty regularly, especially late at night in the office or alone in my home office, I hear a man’s voice, kind of metallic and echoey, commenting on what I’m doing—things like, “Good, keep going, they don’t see it,” or “You’re failing the mission”—even though I know there’s nobody physically there and it’s not coming from the speakers or headset.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.
S021.manifestation: My wife and coworkers tell me that when I try to explain the migration or this cyber threat, I start out making sense but then I jump from firewall rules to Bible verses to youth soccer drills and back to my old college hacking stories, and even I can hear myself trailing off mid‑sentence and never really answering the question they asked.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: When I’m not in that amped‑up mode, it’s like someone turned the color off in my life—I wake up feeling this heavy, gray hopelessness, like nothing I do at work or at church or with my kids is going to matter because I’ve already blown my chance to be who I was supposed to be.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to love hiking with my buddies, tinkering with home servers, and even leading worship at church, but for long stretches now I just sit on the couch staring at my laptop or the wall, ignoring texts and emails, not because I’m busy but because I honestly don’t care enough to move or talk to anybody.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: My eating has been all over the place—during the really wired periods I’ll go a whole day or two barely realizing I haven’t eaten anything but coffee and maybe a protein bar, and then when I crash I’ll just binge on fast food or whatever’s in the house late at night, which is how I ended up dropping weight fast and then putting a bunch of it back on.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: On the down days, I get stuck replaying every mistake from the project and even little things like snapping at my kids, and I honestly feel like the security incident at work, the team’s burnout, and even some of the bad stuff happening in town are somehow my fault, like I’ve cursed everyone by not living up to this role I was given.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: There have been many nights, especially after getting chewed out at work or realizing how much I’ve messed things up at home, where I’ve laid in bed thinking it would be better if I just didn’t wake up, and I’ve caught myself picturing how easy it would be to just drive off the overpass or take all the leftover meds at once, even though I haven’t followed through.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: I swing between feeling unbelievably energized and almost high—like I’m on a mission and everyone should just get out of my way—and then snapping into this sharp, impatient anger when people question me or move too slowly, so minor things at the office or at home can set me off into yelling or slamming doors.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: When I’m in one of those up phases, I can’t sit still: I’ll be pacing between my desk and the server room, rewriting project plans, starting side scripts, texting volunteers about new church tech ideas, and sketching out business ventures all at once, and I get irritated if anyone suggests I take a break.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: For long stretches I’ve been completely convinced that I’m the only person in the company—maybe even in our whole community—who can really see this invisible cyber war going on, like I’ve been specially chosen and wired by God and my experience to protect everyone, and that people who disagree with me just don’t operate on my level of understanding.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: There have been weeks where I’ll sleep two or three hours a night, if that, tinkering with configs, reading security blogs, or sketching flowcharts on the kitchen counter at 3 a.m., and instead of feeling tired I feel almost supercharged, like sleep is a waste of time and my body just doesn’t need it anymore.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My mind gets so revved up that it feels like a dozen browser tabs are open at once and all auto‑refreshing—ideas about the migration, new certifications I should get, ways to overhaul church tech, random childhood memories—all racing so fast that I can’t grab onto one long enough to finish a thought or even follow what someone else is saying to me.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: When I’m like that, I’ll sit down to fix one ticket and instantly get pulled off by a blinking notification, a sound in the hallway, a thought about reorganizing the entire network, or even the pattern in the ceiling tiles, and before I know it I’ve started five different things and finished none of them.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: During the worst of it, I’d load my calendar with back‑to‑back meetings, spin up new pilot projects at work, volunteer for extra committees at church, start an online security blog, and even ramp up sexually with my wife, all at the same time, pacing the house or office when there was the slightest lull because I felt like I had to keep doing something every second.

add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_and_manic_episode_occ: During the height of the migration chaos, when I was sleeping just a couple hours a night and racing around starting new projects, I was also hearing that metallic voice coaching or criticizing me and was convinced leadership had planted bugs to track my every move.
add_requirements.manic_episode_is_present_for_the_majorit: Looking back over these last couple of years, the wired, mission-driven phases where I’m overly energized, taking on too much, and barely sleeping have taken up way more time than the short stretches where I feel closer to my old baseline.
add_requirements.delusions_and_hallucinations_occur_for_2: Even in periods when I’m not especially up or down and just going through the motions at work, I still catch myself hearing that disembodied voice at night and quietly believing certain executives are secretly monitoring me, even though my mood feels more flat than anything.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because of all this, I’ve been written up at work, had key parts of the project taken away from me, pulled back from coaching and church leadership, and my wife has started handling most of the parenting and bills because she doesn’t trust my follow‑through or judgment right now.
add_requirements.duration: This whole roller coaster of extreme highs, crushing lows, and feeling watched has been going on since shortly after I was put in charge of the big IT migration a little over two years ago.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The voice and the fixed belief that certain leaders are secretly monitoring me have been a regular part of my life since about a year and a half after that promotion started to go bad.
add_requirements.manic_episode_duration: The revved‑up, barely-sleeping, overconfident phases started a few months into the migration push and have kept cycling back for well over a year and a half now.
add_requirements.depressive_episode_duration: The stretches of feeling hopeless, guilty, and checked out from things I used to care about have been coming and going for roughly the past seven months.
